text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — severity P1: pod infer-runtime-pod-3 in prod-serving repeatedly restarting (3x) on gpunode-17. Customer 'acme-analytics' reports streaming failures. Link: https://infra.redwood/incident/6078901234

dmitri: seeing OOM during prefill on long-context requests. spikes around 65k tokens. restarting loop started ~00:07 UTC.

eve: thanks — pulling logs now. tagging @oncall and @sre-rotation.

carla: oncall here. what's the immediate customer impact? is streaming failing or timing out?

cust-ops: customer saw partial streams drop and 503s, some sessions ended with reconnect loop. they reported ~10% of requests failing in a 5m window.

alice: kubectl describe pod infer-runtime-pod-3 --namespace=prod-serving shows CrashLoopBackOff, restartCount=3. Node reports GPU mem free low.

alice: logs tail (kubectl logs -p):
```
[2026-03-18T00:06:12Z] ERROR runtime::gpu: CUDA error: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY when allocating 3.2G (requested 3424361984)
[2026-03-18T00:06:12Z] ERROR serve: prefill failed, cancelling stream, reason=oom
[2026-03-18T00:06:12Z] INFO kernel: container exiting with code 137
```

dmitri: yep that's the OOM. this looks correlated with large prefill windows and aggressive kv prefetch. container restarts on oom then k8s restarts it.

sre-rotation: adding mitigation checklist. short plan: 1) immediate: enable model-routing fallback to smaller-context variant for acme-analytics traffic 2) apply emergency limit on max_prefill_tokens to 32k for that route 3) throttle KV prefetch for the service 4) node isolate if noisy neighbor persists.

oncall: I'll execute steps 1 and 2 now. pushing a routing rule: route(acme-analytics) -> model:acme/gpt-xxl-16k-lite (quantized) with max_prefill_tokens=32000.

oncall: done. routing rule active. :white_check_mark:

carla: rolling update to reduce kv prefetch for the runtime: set KV_PREFETCH_BATCH=8 -> applying via config map patch.

alice: patched configmap and restarted deployment pods gracefully (kubectl rollout restart). watching restart counts.

incident-bot: Deployment infer-runtime scaled to 0 -> 2 for graceful restart (automation run id: auto-8247).

eve: monitoring GPU used on gpunode-17 — usage dropped after routing change. no new restarts in last 40s.

cust-ops: told customer we routed them to smaller-context variant and limited very long requests. they're seeing request success rate improve to ~98% now. thanks.

dmitri: need follow-ups: - evaluate whether kv cache eviction tunables caused fragmentation - add guard to prefill path to refuse >48k tokens unless node has >24GB free - add metric for consecutive restart counts per pod to alert earlier.

sre-rotation: already filed follow-up ticket: INF-4521 (prefill-guard, kv-eviction-tune, restart-alert). assigning to eng-runtime.

oncall: marking incident as mitigated for now, but keeping pager open for 2h for regression monitoring.

alice: small note — crash was SIGKILL 137 not cuda illegal instr. looks like kernel OOM. possibly memory spill combined with GPU oom. attaching node diagnostics in ticket.

carla: postmortem req: include examples of offending prompts (redacted), the routing diff, and rollback timeline. will run a canary for the routing change on staging first next deploy.

dmitri: thumbs to ops team :thumbsup:. once stable, we'll roll quantized variant into warmpool and add adaptive throttling during prefill spikes.

incident-bot: Incident P1 status -> mitigated at 00:09:50 UTC. Monitoring window active until 02:09:50 UTC. Incident link: https://infra.redwood/incident/6078901234/details

oncall: closing thread here but keep Slack alerts to #incidents for any new restarts on gpunode-17.

carla: adding notes to customer-facing summary for cust-ops.

cust-ops: customer update sent at 00:12 UTC: "We've routed your traffic to an alternate model and limited extremely long requests while we investigate; no customer data was exposed."

alice: last check — restartCount=0 on affected pods, node memory headroom increased. I'll follow up with logs and flamegraphs in INF-4521.
